Let \(N=|V|=32\), and use the normalized Walsh transform so Fourier projection onto a set \(T\subseteq V^*\) has diagonal entries \(|T|/32\).

If a two-dimensional space \(L\) has support \(S\) and Fourier support \(T\), then \(L\) lies in the intersection of the physical-support subspace on \(S\) and the Fourier-support subspace on \(T\). The standard projection trace argument gives

\[
\dim L\le \frac{|S||T|}{32}.
\]

Since \(\dim L=2\),

\[
|S||T|\ge 64.
\]

So \(U_2^*\ge 64\).

Now construct equality cases. Let \(H\le V\) have dimension \(h\in\{2,3,4\}\), let \(A=c+H\) be a nonzero affine coset not containing \(0\), and choose two distinct nonzero characters \(\eta_1,\eta_2\in H^*\). Define \(L\) on \(A\) by

\[
u_i(c+y)=(-1)^{\eta_i(y)},\qquad y\in H,
\]

and set \(u_i=0\) outside \(A\). Then each \(u_i(0)=0\), and because \(\eta_i\neq0\),

\[
\sum_{x\in V}u_i(x)=0,
\]

so \(L=\langle u_1,u_2\rangle\subseteq \mathcal U\). Here

\[
|S(L)|=|A|=2^h.
\]

The Fourier transform of \(u_i\) is supported on one coset of \(H^\perp\), of size \(2^{5-h}\). The two chosen characters give two distinct such cosets, so

\[
|T(L)|=2\cdot 2^{5-h}=2^{6-h}.
\]

Thus

\[
|S(L)||T(L)|=2^h\cdot 2^{6-h}=64.
\]

Hence \(U_2^*=64\).

It remains to count these equality cases. Equality in the projection trace bound forces exactly the affine-coset construction above: \(S\) must be an affine \(h\)-flat avoiding \(0\), and \(T\) must be the union of two nonzero cosets of \(H^\perp\), for \(h=2,3,4\).

For fixed \(h\):

\[
\#H=\binom{5}{h}_2,
\qquad
\#\text{nonzero cosets}=2^{5-h}-1,
\qquad
\#\{\eta_1,\eta_2\}=\binom{2^h-1}{2}.
\]

So the number is

\[
\sum_{h=2}^4
\binom{5}{h}_2(2^{5-h}-1)\binom{2^h-1}{2}.
\]

Using

\[
\binom52_2=\binom53_2=155,\qquad \binom54_2=31,
\]

we get

\[
155\cdot 7\cdot 3
+
155\cdot 3\cdot 21
+
31\cdot 1\cdot 105
=
3255+9765+3255
=
16275.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{(U_2^*,N_2^*)=(64,16275)}.
\]
